category_title: Adolescent with emotional/behavioral disorder and academic frustration
minimal_context: Isaac is sitting at his desk during class time to complete an independent math quiz on a tablet.
dialogue:
TUTOR: Isaac, it is time for your independent math assignment. Please log into the tablet and complete the quiz questions.

STUDENT: This is a waste of time. I'm not doing these stupid math problems.

TUTOR: You need to finish the assignment. Just do your best.

STUDENT: I can't do it! I don't know these facts! (Scribbles aggressively all over his assignment paper)

TUTOR: Keep trying, Isaac. Look at the next question on the tablet.

STUDENT: I said I'm not doing it! (Grabs the tablet and throws it onto the floor, breaking it, then tears a page out of his math book)

options.A: Instruct the student to use an application like Evernote on the tablet to take notes, organize their daily math work, and archive past assignments and quizzes.
options.B: Implement genuine multicultural math curricula that address race and disability, acknowledging the student's realities, and treating the student as a respected source of knowledge.
options.C: Provide the student with access to similar, but more socially appropriate, sensory stimulation during independent work, such as being given a squishy, stress-relief ball.
options.D: Provide small-group skills practice for 20 minutes daily, including computer-assisted instruction using Math Flash, a mathematics fact family activity, and a 2-minute review of 15 practiced math facts.
